question: Which of the following stages of an automatic transmission system locks the transmission, restricting a vehicle from moving?
solution:
The correct answer is __Park (P) stage****.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Park (P) stage__ is a mode in automatic transmission that locks the transmission.
 
• When in the Park (P) stage, the transmission restricts the vehicle from moving by locking the output shaft of the transmission.
 
• This stage is primarily used when the vehicle is stationary and parked.
 
• The Park (P) stage ensures safety by preventing the vehicle from rolling unintentionally.
 
• It is recommended to always engage the parking brake in conjunction with the Park (P) stage for added security, especially on inclines.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Drive (D) stage:**
 
 
• This stage allows the vehicle to move forward and automatically shifts through the gears.
 
• It is typically used during normal driving conditions.
 
 
 
• **Neutral (N) stage:**
 
 
• In this stage, the transmission is disengaged, and the vehicle can roll freely.
 
• It is often used when the vehicle needs to be pushed or towed.
 
 
 
• **Low (L) stage:**
 
 
• This stage is used for increased engine braking or driving in steep inclines or declines.
 
• It limits the transmission to lower gears for better control and power.
